title: Slab siphon heuristic and tenant-aware kernel negotiation for paged-attention
creator: Micah Nguyen
description: Problem: under high-multiplexing workloads we observe thrashing in the paged KV cache: small tenants with bursty traffic evict hot fragments from larger tenants and kernel choice oscillates causing decode stalls. Goal: introduce a lightweight 'slab siphon' allocation heuristic that (1) biases eviction candidates toward underutilized micro-slabs, (2) enforces per-tenant soft-quotas, and (3) surfaces kernel hint scores to the scheduler so kernel selection can prefer kernels tolerant of fragment sparsity. This ticket prototypes the heuristic, integrates kernel hint feedback, and lands a controlled canary that measures end-to-end decode tail latency and per-token cost.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype deployed behind feature-flag in canary cluster
P95 decode latency for mixed-tenant synthetic workload reduced by >= 15% versus baseline
KV fragmentation (measured by live-fragment-count / allocated-slabs) reduced by >= 20%
No regression (>2%) in steady-state throughput for heavy tenants
Documentation updates (design doc + ops runbook) added to Confluence and linked in ticket
design_notes: Slab siphon: periodically sample slab occupancy and mark low-touch micro-slabs for siphoning rather than immediate eviction to allow batch reclamation with minimal decode interruption.
Tenant-aware soft-quotas: maintain a fast-path approximate LRU per-tenant counter to avoid long-tail eviction of other tenants' hot fragments.
Kernel hint interface: runtime exposes per-fragment sparsity and contiguity score; kernel selector uses a lightweight cost model to prefer sparse-friendly kernels during decode prefill windows.
Fallback behavior: if siphon backlog grows over threshold, force immediate compaction tasks with rate-limited work to avoid memory pressure spikes.
Telemetry: add metrics for siphon queue length, kernel-hint hit-rate, fragment reuse ratio, and tenant-surface-evictions.
Tradeoffs considered: added CPU overhead for siphoning metadata vs. improved decode tail — target budgets set to <2% CPU on host.
Compatibility: feature-flagged and compatible with existing shard soft-isolation mechanisms; does not change on-disk model formats.
implementation_plan: Spike: implement in-memory siphon sampler + small simulation harness (2w)
Integrate kernel-hint producer in prefill path and expose gRPC flag to kernel-selector (1w)
Bench: microbench with synthetic variable-length trace and multi-tenant mix (1w)
Canary rollout (internal zone): run 2% traffic for 48h, collect p95/p99 latency and fragmentation metrics (1w)
Iterate on thresholds and compaction pacing, then expand canary to 10% and schedule broad rollout if metrics pass (1w)
experiment_results: 2026-02-27: Spike sim run (10M tokens): baseline p95 decode 312ms, siphon prototype p95 256ms (-18%), fragmentation ratio 0.61 -> 0.48 (-21%)
2026-03-04: Kernel hint microbench on A100: sparse-kernel path reduced matrix load by ~22% in synthetic sparsity=0.35 traces; end-to-end p50 unchanged, p95 improved by 9%
2026-03-07: CPU overhead measured in spike: siphon metadata sampling consumed ~1.3% host CPU on canary VM, within budget
Notes: observed occasional compaction spikes when siphon backlog hit threshold — added smoothing window to compaction pacing (see comments)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: siphon backlog leading to synchronous compaction and short-term latency spikes. Mitigation: rate-limited compaction worker + emergency pressure breaker that drains oldest siphon entries first.

Risk: kernel hint inaccuracies could cause suboptimal kernel selection on unseen model topologies. Mitigation: roll out kernel hints as advisory only; maintain conservative cost weights and collect offline model-specific calibration.
Risk: cross-tenant fairness regressions. Mitigation: enforce soft-quotas with exponential backoff and add alerting for tenant eviction spikes.
